issues.legal_issue: A court should preserve the nature and status quo of disputed property during a pending suit unless a party seeking to change it establishes irreparable loss or damage.
material_facts: A suit for possession was pending, and the claimant obtained a temporary injunction restraining the opposing party from alienating the property or constructing on it.

The appellate court permitted alienation subject to the law governing transfers during litigation and construction at the opposing party’s risk; the High Court dismissed the revision after recording an undertaking concerning alienation, construction, and future tenants.

The opposing party relied on the anticipated length of the proceedings and the desire to put the property to better use, but did not establish irreparable loss or damage or an extraordinary ground for changing the property.
The Court restored the trial court’s injunction.
issues.conclusion: The appellate court and the High Court were not justified in permitting construction or alienation without an established case of irreparable loss or damage or an extraordinary ground. Their orders were set aside, and the trial court’s injunction was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 39 Rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the court may grant temporary injunctive relief. During pending litigation, the nature of disputed property should not be changed, including by construction or alienation, unless irreparable loss or damage is established. The prospect of lengthy proceedings or a desire to put the property to better use is not enough. If the claim ultimately fails, damages may be claimed or awarded. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: pending_property_suit and proposed_change_to_disputed_property and not irreparable_loss_or_damage_shown

predicates.pending_property_suit: A party has brought a suit concerning rights to property, and the suit remains pending.
predicates.proposed_change_to_disputed_property: A party proposes to alter the disputed property’s nature or status, including through construction or alienation.
predicates.irreparable_loss_or_damage_shown: The party seeking the change has established that refusing it would cause irreparable loss or damage.

issues.definition: When a property suit is pending and a party proposes to change the disputed property, the change should be prohibited if irreparable loss or damage has not been shown.
